structure.text: The storm creates groups whose encounters Prospero can arrange while controlling what each knows.

structure.title: A shared scene
structure.text: The final gathering brings separate experiences together, testing what can be acknowledged in another person's presence.

context.title: Rival accounts of the island
context.text: Prospero's story of injury is not the only claim to legitimacy. Caliban speaks of prior possession, while Ariel recalls a promise of freedom.
context.takeaway: Hear the servants' accounts as well.

context.title: Theatre inside theatre
context.text: Music, apparitions, and staged scenes arrange what the visitors feel. Prospero resembles a director, but his performers have wishes of their own.
context.takeaway: Control depends on other people's work.

opening: Prospero has spent years on an island with his daughter, remembering the brother who stole his position and sent them out to sea. Now his enemies are sailing past, and he has learned enough magic to bring their ship within reach. He can separate them, frighten them, and arrange what they see. Shakespeare gives an injured man extraordinary control over the people who wronged him, then lets the business of settling accounts compete with his daughter's discovery of a life beyond her father.
